banh-mi-trung.name: Vietnamese egg bánh mì
banh-mi-trung.description: A hot, crispy loaf of bread sandwiched with a soft fried egg, cucumber and carrot pickles; familiar breakfast dish, easy to make at home.
banh-mi-trung.serving_basis: Two bánh mì rolls, one per person, with egg and pickled vegetables.
banh-mi-trung.finished_dish: A crisp baguette with fragrant soft egg, cool cucumber and sweet-sour carrot for balance.
banh-mi-trung.serving: Serve while the bread is crisp. For a vegan version, replace the egg with pan-seared tofu.
banh-mi-trung.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Gently squeeze the carrots after pickling so the bread does not become wet.
Use just enough soy sauce and serve chili on the side so everyone can adjust the heat.

preparation_steps: Shred the carrot, toss it with vinegar, sugar and chili, and leave for 15 minutes to mellow; squeeze lightly to drain.
Rinse and slice the cucumber; pick the cilantro leaves. Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Slit the baguettes lengthwise and warm them briefly. Mince the garlic and mix it into the soy sauce.
cooking_steps: Heat half the oil in a pan, pour in the eggs and cook into a thin omelet; turn, cook until just set and fold.
Open the baguettes and layer in the egg, cucumber, pickled carrot and cilantro. Drizzle with a little soy sauce, add chili to taste and serve immediately.

lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.name: Phu Yen chicken hotpot with Vietnamese basil
lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.description: Hot pot of chicken fragrant with eu leaves, cooked with bamboo shoots and mushrooms; dish associated with Phu Yen, often eaten with fresh vermicelli and herbs.
lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.serving_basis: One hotpot for four, including the bones and broth.
lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.finished_dish: A naturally sweet chicken broth scented with peppery Vietnamese basil, crisp bamboo shoots and tender mushrooms, served hot with rice vermicelli.
lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.serving: Keep the hotpot at a gentle simmer, add the basil a little at a time, and serve with fresh rice vermicelli.
lau-ga-la-e-phu-yen.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Fresh bamboo shoots need to be boiled and rinsed first; pre-cooked shoots may need less time.
Add the basil at the end or dip it into the simmering pot to preserve its aroma.

preparation_steps: Clean the chicken and cut it into serving pieces. Rub gently with salt and ginger, rinse and drain.
Slice the bamboo shoots, boil and rinse them several times; trim the tough ends from the mushrooms.
Remove wilted basil leaves, rinse gently and drain; reserve the tender leaves for dipping. Bruise the lemongrass and chili.
cooking_steps: Marinate the chicken with fish sauce, salt, lemongrass and some of the chili for 20 minutes.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil until fragrant. Stir-fry the chicken until sealed, then add water, lemongrass and the remaining chili. Bring to a boil and lower the heat.
Simmer for about 30 minutes until the chicken is tender. Add the bamboo shoots and cook for 10 minutes, then add the mushrooms and adjust the seasoning.
Set the hotpot over a table burner and dip in the basil a little at a time. Serve hot with vermicelli; avoid simmering the basil for long.

banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.name: Hoi An vegetarian bánh xèo
banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.description: Small pancakes with crispy golden edges, filled with mushrooms, tofu and bean sprouts; Serve hot with raw vegetables, rice paper and sweet and sour soy sauce.
banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.serving_basis: Four small portions, one or two pancakes each depending on pan size.
banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.finished_dish: Thin golden pancakes with crisp edges, tender fragrant mushroom and tofu filling, and crunchy bean sprouts.
banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.serving: Wrap pieces of pancake with fresh herbs in rice paper and dip in soy sauce. For a vegan meal, check that all seasonings are animal-free.
banh-xeo-chay-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Rest the batter and stir it again before each pancake.
Use a hot pan with a thin film of oil and avoid overfilling.
Use soy sauce instead of fish sauce; check the label of any premixed batter.

preparation_steps: Whisk the batter with coconut milk, water, turmeric and salt until smooth; rest for 20 minutes.
Shred the mushrooms and gently press the tofu before cutting it into strips; rinse the bean sprouts. Finely slice the scallions, rinse the herbs and drain.
Mix the soy sauce with lime, sugar and minced chili; balance it to a gentle sweet-sour taste.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots in a little oil until fragrant, then stir-fry the mushrooms and tofu until just firm. Set aside.
Heat a small pan and brush with a thin layer of oil. Stir the batter, pour in enough to coat the pan thinly, then add the mushroom, tofu and sprouts to one half.
Cover for 1–2 minutes, then uncover and cook over medium heat until the edges crisp. Fold in half and transfer to a plate; repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve hot with fresh herbs, rice paper and soy dipping sauce. Wrap bite-sized portions.

cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.name: Cao Lau Vegetarian Hoi An
cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.description: Tough Cao Lau fibers served with green vegetables, mushrooms and vegetable protein simmered in soy sauce; Add a little sauce to keep the dry mixed dish of Hoi An.
cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.serving_basis: 4 medium bowls; Reduce fiber if used as a dish in a multi-course meal.
cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.finished_dish: Chewy noodles, fresh green vegetables, mushrooms and vegetarian ribs rich in soy sauce; The sauce is just enough, the ram cake stays crispy.
cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.serving: Serve in a bowl with green vegetables, bean sprouts, ram cake and a little simmering sauce; Use immediately after mixing.
cao-lau-chay-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Choose Cao Lau fibers with ingredients suitable for vegetarians; Vegetarian mushroom sauce instead of regular oyster sauce.
Don't add too much broth: Cao Lau is a mixed dish with little sauce.
Just break the ram cake before eating to keep it crispy.

preparation_steps: Soak vegetarian short ribs according to package instructions, squeeze dry; Thickly sliced ​​mushrooms.
Wash vegetables and bean sprouts and drain. Separating Cao Lau fibers; Steam or blanch quickly according to the fiber's instructions.
Mince garlic, chop green onions; Mix soy sauce, vegetarian mushroom sauce and sugar with coconut water.
cooking_steps: Pan-fry the vegetarian short ribs until lightly golden, then take them out; fry garlic until fragrant.
Put the mushrooms on the island, add vegetarian ribs and a mixture of coconut water and soy sauce; Simmer over low heat until the sauce coats the ingredients.
Divide vegetables and bean sprouts into the bottom of the bowl, place Cao Lau on top; Add mushrooms, vegetarian ribs and a little simmering sauce.
Sprinkle with green onions, add chili as desired and break the ram cake onto the surface. Mix lightly when eating.

va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.name: Fig mixed with Hue vegetarian flowers
va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.description: Lightly boiled figs mixed with tofu, mushrooms, vegetables and herbs; Mild sour and salty taste, served with crispy rice paper according to Hue vegetarian dishes.
va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.serving_basis: 4 side dishes; Set the rice paper aside to crisp up.
va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.finished_dish: The soft and fleshy fig pieces are still intact, mixed with a mild sour and salty taste; Tofu and mushrooms make the dish more flavorful, and herbs keep the smell fresh.
va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.serving: Serve as a side dish or vegetarian mix; scoop with rice paper. Set aside rice paper, peanuts and sesame until serving time.
va-tron-hoa-mau-chay-hue.time_note: Total time includes operation and waiting time; Actual time depends on the kitchen and the size of the ingredients.
tips: Let the figs cool and the ingredients dry before mixing so the dish doesn't become mushy.
Add water and mix a little at a time; The astringency and moistness of figs varies with age.
Mix close to mealtime; Keep the rice paper, peanuts and sesame seeds separate for crunchiness.

Soak the mushrooms until they bloom, wash them and then slice them. Sliced ​​carrots and cucumbers; Wash and chop herbs.
Cut tofu into small pieces, saute until golden. Mix soy sauce, lemon, sugar, minced ginger and chili into a mixture.
cooking_steps: Stir-fry a little ginger, add mushrooms and stir-fry quickly until cooked; let it cool down.
Mix figs with tofu, mushrooms, carrots and cucumbers. Sprinkle with water and mix a little at a time, stir gently and taste again.
